READ (any accepted seat): info → CMS/PHP/component versions · content.list {kind, search, offset, limit≤200, include_body} → one page of records; search:"<part of the title>" keeps the rows whose title, alias or slug holds it (Joomla 0.20.0+, WordPress 0.16.0+; an older one answers LIST_SEARCH_UNSUPPORTED, whose next is the road). kind ∈ {article, articleAssociation, category, tag, field, fieldValue, menuItem, menuAssociation, menutype, module, moduleAssignment, templateStyle, language, languageFilter, redirect, banner, bannerClient, contact, newsfeed, user, extensionParams, post, postmeta, option, templatePart, term} · content.get {kind, id | key} → one full record · content.replace {find, replace, path?, where?, all?, changes?, dryRun?} → changes words already on this site in one call, where the site has it; its answer is the receipt with its undo · content.read {type?, locale?, limit?, cursor?} → authenticated tracy-content/v1 live summaries; {id, blocksCursor?} reads detail; {id, blockId, blocksCursor?} reads one block. Available only when the Claude Cowork plugin supports it. Follow links.next, keep filters unchanged, restart on CONTENT_SNAPSHOT_EXPIRED. A 413 on bodyHtml carries error.links.firstBlock: pass its id/blockId/blocksCursor query to read the page block by block. Partial/unresolved data is explicit; reading a field does not authorize writing it. Use fresh native inspect for writes. · An option is addressed by NAME: content.get {kind:"option", key:"<option_name>"} reads it and content.update {kind:"option", key, fields:{value:"…"}} writes it; on WordPress content.list lists posts only. Never write an option in order to discover what it was. · extension.list (Joomla) · plugin.list, theme.list (WordPress) · db.tables · core.manifest · media.scan {limit≤100} → the largest images in the webroot with width/height and public URL (runs in the lane, not via the site) · media.draw {prompt, slot? | like? | aspect?} → {path, width, height, next}: DRAWS a new picture from your prompt with the picture model /ops assigned and uploads it to the media library as the person you work with. page.text: the words a visitor reads on a page of THIS site, as served now. Use it to find where a text is, a page's parts when the customer names a position, or its SEO tags. Not after a words write (its answer is the check); not for looks (page.look), sections or the page list (content.read {view:"pages"}). Call {path:"/", match?, maxChars?:≤8000, outline?:true, head?:true, paths?:[…≤8]}. Returns {url, lang, title, text}, text ≤2,000 chars unless maxChars; match keeps the lines holding it ("@" for e-mails, a few digits for a phone) plus pictures:[{near, src}] in their card; outline: one line per part, "<topbar|header|main|footer> <h1|p|button|nav|logo|text>: words [href]"; head: description, robots, canonical, og, hreflang, jsonLd, headings, alt-less images; robots.txt or a sitemap reads as lines; paths: {pages:[…]}. Answers come back as the seat book and the component return them: {ok:true, …} or {ok:false, code|error, …}; a refusal that carries next says what to do instead. COMPONENT_NOT_REGISTERED means this site is not connected yet; NO_VIEWER means nobody has this site open in a browser. Content written here is stored in the site database and is not a file commit; file changes still go through the webroot.

Returns {file, url, description?}: follow its next · style: each prop's value, rule and var(--token) source · the largest images {path, url, width, height} · {path}. Effects: media.draw adds ONE picture per call: apply its path to the slot. Refusals: NO_BROWSER → page.text.
content.contract: reads and changes this quickstart site slot by slot. Use when content.replace cannot: a picture, a link, words it refused. Not for structure or settings (content.update) or a read-only question (content.read). Call: after content.read showed the slot (field.next), ONE {operation:"apply", changes:{"<slot key>":"<value>", …}} carrying every change — no inspect, Tracy sends the revisions it read; a slot marked requiresEvidence also takes evidence:{"<key>":"<the customer's words>"}. Only when content.read did not show the slot: {operation:"inspect", page, slots:"text", match} (10–20 s at first), then apply with expected_revision:<its revision>. Leave apply_id and request_id out: Tracy makes a pair per apply (an apply_id you give starts "contract-" and is new). An answer's `normalized` lists what Tracy corrected in your call: use that form next time. A slot's language: the site context's rule. Apart from Site identity, an occupied slot cannot be emptied and an empty one cannot be filled; nothing is created or deleted. Returns the apply's receipt: read nothing afterwards. Pictures: media.draw {prompt, slot}, then apply the path. Languages: content.contract {operation:"multilingual.retire", keep:[<tags to keep>], apply_id:"mlang-<new>"} hides the rest (repeat until completed); tracy_site_build_joomla request language.add adds one. Undo: apply.revert {apply_id} (the latest contract apply; a retire: multilingual.restore, same id). Refusals: contract_failed → its next; writer_busy → Tracy already retried: tell the customer.
content.update · content.delete: add, edit, move or trash one record of THIS site. Use when settings change or content.replace cannot. Not for words the software prints (content.find). Call content.update {kind, id, fields, apply_id} — id left out (or 0) CREATES one; on an existing record parent_id / move_after MOVE it with everything under it; fields.params (or attribs, images, urls, metadata) as {patch:{…}} merges into the stored column (null removes a key; a key held as JSON text (jatools-config) is patched as an object, never re-typed) · content.delete {kind, id, apply_id}. apply_id names the receipt: one per item of the request. Returns {kind, id, created}: the receipt. Effects: live at once; a delete TRASHES (nothing is purged); apply.revert {apply_id} undoes that item, an insert included. Refusals: a kind that cannot be created or moved is refused by name.
site.identity: THIS site's name, its description and whether page titles carry the name — one value for every page (Joomla's global configuration). Use when the customer renames the site, or the name every page shows in the browser tab or the header. Not for a heading of one page (content.replace). Call {operation:"read"} · {operation:"set", fields:{sitename?, MetaDesc?, sitename_pagetitles?:0|1|2}}. Returns {fields, changed}: the receipt; normalized names its apply_id. Effects: live on every page at once; apply.revert {apply_id} undoes it. Refusals: unsupported → only those three fields.
apply.revert · apply.list: undo one apply, or say what it changed. Use when the customer asks to undo a change, or what one did. Not for words (content.update); apply.list never after a write: the write's answer is the receipt; with no apply_id before any write: the site's recent changes. Call apply.revert {apply_id} · apply.list {apply_id?}. Returns {reverted} · {apply_id, steps}. Effects: apply.revert undoes one apply to the byte.
db.snapshot · db.rollback · db.tables · db.dump · core.manifest · extension.install · extension.enable · core.upgrade: what THIS site RUNS. Use when installing or upgrading. Not for content or reading it: content.get/list, never db.dump. Call db.snapshot {tables?} FIRST · db.rollback {tag} · db.dump {table, limit?, cursor?} · extension.install {url:"https://….zip"} (the site downloads it; no uninstall) · extension.enable {type, element, folder?, enabled, apply_id} · core.upgrade {to:"4.4"|"5.4"|"6.1", step:"prepare"|"finalise"}: ONE hop, two separate calls. Returns {tag} from db.snapshot. Effects: live at once; db.rollback {tag} undoes. Refusals: dump_failed → db.tables for the real name.
Tiers: reads run freely; writes run at once, undoably, but hiding, site-wide, 6+ places or money ask too; content.delete takes every language of a record unless locale names one; destructive (media.delete, content.delete, db.rollback, extension.install, extension.enable, core.upgrade, multilingual.retire): call first; CONFIRM_FIRST gives the one question, then the same call with confirm:true.

apply.revert · apply.list: undo one apply, or say what it changed. Use when the customer asks to undo a change, or what one did. Effects: writes the record showing the words; dryRun (needs replace) writes nothing; undo: the answer's, as given. Refusals: AMBIGUOUS → at:[…]; NOT_FOUND → page.text {match}, quote exactly; NOT_EDITABLE → tell the customer why.
page.create: a new page and its menu link in one call, in the theme's own markup. Use when the customer asks for a new page. Not for an existing one (content.replace). Effects: live at once. Refusals: NOT_FOUND or AMBIGUOUS list the menus to name.
content.list · content.get · info · plugin.list · theme.list: THIS site's records as stored. Use when a question needs stored fields. Not for words (content.contract, page.text) or the page list (content.read {view:"pages"}). A body (post_content, a part's content) goes by blocks: content.get {…, outline:true} numbers them, with rev (always over 16,000 chars), block:i reads one; {rev, blocks:{"<i>":"<markup>"|null, "+<i>":"<markup>"|{pattern:"<name>"}}} changes, drops or adds just those; a key may be a block's own metadata.name, a value {find,replace} (find stands once in it) or {attrs:{…}} (metadata, lock; any attr of a /--> block; null removes one). In fields: the WHOLE body (shorter: BODY_SHRINK). Returns {kind, id, key, created, verified}: the receipt. Effects: live at once; apply.revert undoes it.
content.delete · content.language · language.install · apply.revert · apply.list: delete, translate, undo. Use when a page goes, a language comes or a change is undone. Not for words (content.update); apply.list never after a write: the write's answer is the receipt; with no apply_id before any write: the site's recent changes. Call content.delete {kind:"post", id} · content.language {id, lang, translations?:{<lang>:<id>}} · language.install {locale} · apply.revert {apply_id} · apply.list {apply_id?}. apply_id is optional: left out, Tracy makes one per write. Returns receipts; apply.list {apply_id, steps}. Effects: a delete trashes; apply.revert undoes one apply to the byte.
theme.install · theme.activate · theme.style · plugin.install · plugin.activate · db.tables · db.dump · core.manifest: what THIS site RUNS. Use when installing a theme or plugin. Not for content or reading it (content.get/list). Call db.dump {table, limit?, cursor?} · theme.install | plugin.install {url:"https://….zip"} · theme.activate {stylesheet} · theme.style {style} · plugin.activate {file:"<dir>/<file>.php"}; install, then activate: two calls. Returns the receipt. Effects: live at once. Refusals: dump_failed → db.tables for the real name.
Tiers: reads run freely; writes run at once, undoably, but hiding, site-wide, 6+ places or money ask too; content.delete takes every language of a record unless locale names one; destructive (media.delete, content.delete, theme.install, theme.activate, plugin.install, plugin.activate): call first; CONFIRM_FIRST gives the one question, then the same call with confirm:true.
A refusal's next is the fix; a toolset it names is the role the customer needs. Content written here is in the site database, not a file commit.

action.description: An action the description gives the rules of.

params.description: That action's parameters, as its line shows them.

comment.description: The number of the person's comment this call answers, or [1, 2] for several; the write is made for whoever commented.

tools.name: tracy_emdash
tools.door: The EmDash site's own MCP server (`/_emdash/api/mcp`), reached inside the site's container with the viewer's token; not the Apply door.
tools.description: Words on a page: tracy_site content.replace {find, replace}. Labels: not writable. WORDS — read the entry first: `content_get {collection, id:<slug>}` for a page or the site-wide `site` entry, `content_list {collection}` for a list; the locale is filled with this site's own language — pass `locale` for another. Then ONE `content_update {collection, id:<the id it answered>, data:{only the fields you change}, status:"published"}` (no `_rev`) changes AND publishes; its answer is the receipt. Leave `status` out only to stage a draft; `status:"draft"` takes a live page off the site. A list field takes {"<index>":{changed keys}}; null drops it, "+":[…] appends. Menus: menu_get → menu_set_items. Redirects: redirect_create {source, destination, type:301|302}, redirect_list, redirect_delete {id}. Verification tags: settings_update {seo:{googleVerification…}}; entry seo panels never show. No rebuild. Forms: form_list, form_words. Pictures: the customer's → tracy_site media.upload {file} (Files tab) | {attachment} (in chat) → its id into the field. content_update edits/removes page image refs. media_delete removes library record + stored file; refs can break. It cannot revoke public URLs or purge edge caches; caches may still serve. {list:true, tools:[names]}: schemas. CONFLICT → content_get for a fresh _rev; PENDING_DRAFT and CONFIRM_FIRST (content_delete {collection, id}: ONE call, all languages unless locale names one; call first) → ask_user_question, its ask only, then confirm:true.

tool.description: An EmDash MCP tool name, e.g. content_update.

arguments.description: That tool's own arguments, as EmDash names them; this tool's description gives the content ones.

list.description: true → one line per tool this site publishes; with tools, those tools' full argument schemas.

tools.description: With list: the tool names whose schemas you need.

confirm.description: true → what the customer agreed to after CONFIRM_FIRST or PENDING_DRAFT and their answer.

allLocales.description: true → a read covers every language (large); never on a write.

raw.description: true → EmDash's answer unshaped: every column, full schemas.

siteKey.description: Leave this out: every call acts on this conversation's site (/site/<label>); naming another site is refused.

comment.description: The number of the person's comment this call answers, or [1, 2] for several; the write is made for whoever commented.

otherTools.name: tracy_brand
otherTools.description: The customer's brand as their live site shows it — colours, fonts, logo, tagline, sample images — or any public site's, as a design template of its own: `brand:<host>`. action="read" (url default: this site) → {manifest, brand, material}; NOT_EXTRACTED → extract it first. action="extract" measures it (4–10 s); one measured in the last 30 days comes back as it stands, `reused: true`, unless refresh. pages:true also crawls its pages ("Fork a site"): write the customer's own pages from that list, never the source's words. action="list" → every extracted brand. Refusals: BAD_URL (not a public site), NO_MATERIAL (could not be fetched from here: say so, offer to look in the browser). How it feeds a redesign: the tracy-design-inspiration skill.

otherTools.name: tracy_design_copy
otherTools.description: Write the customer's words into a design template's layout: a PREVIEW version in the Design templates dialog, never a change to the live site ("the pricing page in Stripe" is one). action="form" {id, chip} → that chip's slots and the length each allows; action="write" {id, chip, lang, slots, title?} stores one version, in the site's language; a text over its slot's length is refused by name. Workflow: the tracy-design-inspiration skill.

otherTools.name: tracy_design_library
otherTools.description: The design template catalog (no id), or one design template's DESIGN.md and tokens.css (id); read at most three. Files live in Tracy, not in the shell. While design systems are off it answers with the published templates instead. Workflow: the tracy-design-inspiration skill.

otherTools.name: tracy_design_propose
otherTools.description: Show one to three design templates for THIS site, drawn live on its own content: the chat renders the cards, never describe or paste them. Each pick is a catalog id (tracy_design_library) or brand:<host> (tracy_brand) with one line of why in the customer's words — one keeps the current spirit, one upgrades it, one is bold; a named one alone. Workflow: the tracy-design-inspiration skill.

otherTools.name: tracy_find_definition
otherTools.description: Find which PHP file defines a named CMS thing — a post type, taxonomy, shortcode, block, option or hook — and return the file and line. Read-only. Prefer this over a glob-and-grep crawl: it skips uploads, vendor and cache, so it neither misses must-use plugins nor blows the subprocess output cap.

otherTools.name: tracy_site_profile
otherTools.description: Identify the CMS in the site webroot and report its shape: platform, version, table prefix, themes, plugins and must-use plugins. Read-only. Call this before reasoning about where anything lives — guessing the platform from a directory name is the usual way to be wrong.
